name: JWT credential insufficiently protected
description:
A JSON Web Token that the server verifies is a bearer credential: whoever holds the string acts as the user it was issued to, until it expires. The application carries or stores such a token where parties other than the server and the user's own browser can read it: in the request URL, where it is kept in browser history and server and proxy logs and sent onward in the Referer header; in a cookie set without the HttpOnly attribute, where any script running on the origin can read it, so a single cross-site scripting flaw anywhere on the site steals the session; in a cookie set without the Secure attribute, which the browser also sends over plain HTTP; or over an unencrypted connection, where anyone on the network path can read and replay it.

burpsy reports this only when the token is shown to be a credential: the captured request was replayed with the token's signature altered and with the token removed, and both were answered differently from the original, which was itself a success; the altered token and the original were each sent a second time with the same result. A JWT-shaped value the server does not verify is not reported by this row.

This row is burpsy's own: Burp's issue catalogue has no entry for it.
remediation: Carry session JWTs only in an HttpOnly, Secure cookie (with SameSite) or in an Authorization header held in memory, and only over HTTPS. Never put a token in a URL. Do not store tokens in localStorage or sessionStorage. Keep token lifetimes short and support revocation so a leaked token stops working.
